req.title: Task ids are monotonically increasing
req.statement: The system shall assign strictly increasing integer ids to newly created tasks.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that task ids must be strictly increasing integers. To verify this, we need: (1) a positive test confirming two sequential tasks have strictly increasing ids, (2) a boundary test confirming the id of the second task is exactly id_first + 1 (not +2 or equal), and (3) a negative test confirming that a single task creation returns a valid integer id (baseline), plus an additional test verifying that creating N tasks yields a strictly monotonically increasing sequence. We use an in-memory SQLite database via dependency override to ensure isolation and determinism. Tests assert exact values to catch off-by-one and comparison-operator mutations.

tests.name: test_two_sequential_tasks_have_strictly_increasing_ids
expected: id of Task B is strictly greater than id of Task A
id of Task B equals id of Task A + 1
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from app.main import app
from app.database import get_db, Base

def test_two_sequential_tasks_have_strictly_increasing_ids():
    engine = create_engine("sqlite:///:memory:", connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})
    Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
    TestingSessionLocal = sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine)
    def override_get_db():
        db = TestingSessionLocal()
        try:
            yield db
        finally:
            db.close()
    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db
    client = TestClient(app)
    r1 = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Task A", "completed": False})
    r2 = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Task B", "completed": False})
    assert r1.status_code == 201
    assert r2.status_code == 201
    id1 = r1.json()["id"]
    id2 = r2.json()["id"]
    assert isinstance(id1, int)
    assert isinstance(id2, int)
    assert id2 > id1
    assert id2 == id1 + 1
    app.dependency_overrides.clear()

test_two_sequential_tasks_have_strictly_increasing_ids()

Verify each consecutive pair is strictly increasing

tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from app.main import app
from app.database import get_db, Base

def test_five_sequential_tasks_form_strictly_increasing_sequence():
    engine = create_engine("sqlite:///:memory:", connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})
    Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
    TestingSessionLocal = sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine)
    def override_get_db():
        db = TestingSessionLocal()
        try:
            yield db
        finally:
            db.close()
    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db
    client = TestClient(app)
    ids = []
    for i in range(5):
        r = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": f"Task {i}", "completed": False})
        assert r.status_code == 201
        ids.append(r.json()["id"])
    for idx in range(1, len(ids)):
        assert ids[idx] > ids[idx - 1]
        assert ids[idx] == ids[idx - 1] + 1
    assert ids == sorted(ids)
    assert len(set(ids)) == 5
    app.dependency_overrides.clear()
